newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ILO wants to stop kids making soccer balls.
newsitem.headline: ILO wants to stop kids making soccer balls.

text.p: The U.N. labour body and sports goods giants joined forces on Friday to try to stop child labour in Pakistan, where at least 7,000 children work full time stitching two-thirds of the world's soccer balls.

The International Labour Organisation, in a statement issued in Geneva, said it signed an agreement with makers like Adidas, Nike and Reebok and industrialists in Pakistan to remove child labourers from the industry.

The city of Sialkot, the centre of Pakistan's sports goods industry, produces two-thirds of the world's hand-stitched soccer balls for an export market worth $1 billion a year in retail sales, the ILO said.

Under the deal, signed in Atlanta, the ILO will help soccer ball manufacturers to remove child labourers from their work with the help of financing from the U.S. government and the Soccer Industry Council of America.

The International Federation of Football Associations (FIFA) hailed the agreement, the latest step by Pakistan to curb child labour which has drawn scathing international criticism and threats of trade sanctions.

"While we've been concerned about the negative publicity created for football by reports of child labour...our main concern has of course been to help solve the problem itself," said FIFA General Secretary Joseph Blatter.

In Pakistan, the ILO will cooperate with Sialkot's Chamber of Commerce and Industry to monitor the industry, increase awareness of child labour among producers and assist children removed from the workplace, its statement said.
